findings.analysis: Spec authority (issue #2 amendment, refs/forge/issues/2, comment b79a87e): clause 1 allows 'run the CI plan against the result tree, or prove result tree == the tree CI checked' (verify_result_ci implements this). Clause 2: 'A review decision must be bound to the result being merged'. Clause 3: 'no path merges an unreviewed or unchecked result'. The reviewer's case: the same approval is accepted for --merge/--squash/--rebase; the result-tree CI run is unrecorded and cannot make the earlier review authorize the result; a merger can silently choose a different result-producing strategy while the gate passes. Primary-source facts: (1) on an UNMOVED base, all four strategies produce result tree == source tree (merge commit tree == squash tree == rebase replay tree == ff source tree; base is an ancestor), so tree-equality proof covers every strategy; (2) on a MOVED base (the live-base #2 path), the result tree genuinely differs from the source tree, so the strategy and the materialized result identity are NOT covered by an input-bound approve + source check. Therefore the exact-result binding is required exactly on the moved-base path. KEY CONSTRAINT: VAL-207's evidence 'fresh CI+review 后通过' and the reviewer's own summary ('VAL-207's two-PR happy/refusal path ... are present, but integration is blocked') plus the acceptance flow in tests/t3_merge.rs:4729-4734 (fresh ci + plain `pr review --approve` then `pr merge` expects exit 0) and adapter devflow.cjs:2170/2553 (`pr review <id> --approve` then `pr merge <id> --ff`; adapter is out of scope / must not be altered). This is the core tension: pre-materialization approval cannot literally record a result commit that does not exist yet; the acceptance flow is a single merge invocation after one approve.
findings.decisionQuestion: For moved-base (live-base) merges, how must the approval bind to the materialized result? Choose minimal alternative below; each is a user-visible flow change that must be approved by the user (adapter flow `review --approve` then `merge --ff` stays valid under all four because ff result == source tree → tree-equality proof covers it).

alternatives.userVisibleFlow: Live-base merges require the approval to name the strategy: `git forge pr review <n> --approve --strategy merge|squash|rebase|ff`. `pr merge <n> --<strategy>` on a moved base then requires the effective review's bound strategy to EQUAL the requested strategy; mismatch refuses with a re-review remedy (re-approve with the matching --strategy). Unmoved-base merges keep legacy plain approve (tree equality proves the result tree == tree CI checked, so any strategy's content is the reviewed tree). pr.merge event already records {strategy, result_commit}; optionally also record result_tree. Existing live-base tests + dogfood gain `--strategy` on the fresh approve; all unmoved-base tests and the adapter stay byte-identical.
alternatives.satisfies: Clause 2 (review bound to the result via deterministic strategy+source+base inputs, with the materialized tree CI-proved equal or re-run); reviewer's 'same approval accepted for all strategies' closed on the moved-base path; VAL-207 passes (fresh CI + fresh strategy-bound approve → merge passes, one invocation); adapter untouched.
alternatives.cost: CLI surface: pr review gains --strategy; gate enforces equality; 3-4 t3 tests + dogfood live-base section gain the flag. About 60-100 lines + tests.

alternatives.id: ALT-2 post-materialization re-review (reviewer's literal suggested fix)
alternatives.userVisibleFlow: Moved-base merge materializes the result FIRST, pins it (pending result ref + result identity = strategy+commit+tree), and REFUSES the merge until a fresh result-bound review (and result-bound CI check) is recorded against that exact identity; the finalize only accepts a candidate whose identity exactly equals the recorded one. Unmoved-base merges need no re-review (tree equality). Adapter --ff path unaffected.
alternatives.satisfies: Reviewer's literal 'record it on both the successful Check and approving Review, and require exact equality with the candidate passed to finalize; otherwise require re-review after materialization'.
alternatives.cost: Changes the acceptance/dogfood live-base flow to TWO merge invocations with an intermediate result-bound approve+ci (tests/t3_merge.rs:4729-4734, dogfood lb section, live_base_merge_requires_each_gate_input_rebound ALL change shape); merge command grows a resume/finalize-on-pinned-result mode; new CLI surface (review/ci bound to the pending result; merge resume). Significantly larger; conflicts with the reviewer's own 'VAL-207 path is present' stance and with 'single approve then merge passes' reading of the ticket acceptance.

alternatives.id: ALT-3 hybrid: strategy-bound review + strategy/result recorded on pr.merge + result-tree CI recorded as a result-bound ci.check in the finalize transaction
alternatives.userVisibleFlow: Same as ALT-1 (moved-base approve must carry --strategy), plus the finalize transaction atomically writes a result-bound ci.check event (status, plan, generation, base_head, strategy, result_commit) as an intermediate parent of the pr.merge event, so the 'successful Check' is ALSO recorded bound to the materialized result identity. This is ALT-1 + the full 'record it on both' ask.
alternatives.satisfies: ALT-1 + reviewer's 'record it on both the successful Check and approving Review'.
alternatives.cost: ALT-1 + finalize transaction change (write two unappended event commits in one update-ref batch; head CAS parent chain: head_expected → result ci.check → pr.merge). Moderate extra complexity; must keep VAL-208 atomicity tests green (nothing applied on CAS failure — the extra commit is dangling on failure, refs unchanged).

findings.recommendation: ALT-3 if the user accepts a moved-base flow where the approving review must name the strategy; ALT-1 if minimality dominates. Explicitly recommended NOT to ship the current behavior (unbound approval valid for moved-base results) — that is exactly F-002's unresolved defect.
